title: Competitor deployment runway and prioritized research sprint
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary: This ticket scopes a focused research sprint to productize a 'deployment runway' that maps competitor model availability, quantized performance profiles, and procurement triggers into prioritized experiments. The goal is to produce a defensible prioritized backlog (50% research, 50% validation) that informs model fallback policies, Dedicated capacity procurement signals, and Console alerts for customers.

Context: We continue to see frequent supplier cadence changes and model variant launches that affect cost and latency arbitrage. Instead of ad-hoc reactions, PM & Research should own a reproducible runway model: (1) signal ingestion, (2) scenario generation (availability windows, pricing shocks, latency degradation), (3) experiment matrix (latency, cost, quality trade-offs), and (4) prioritized playbook for rollouts and customer communications.
acceptance_criteria: Scorecard prototype that ranks 25 candidate models by availability risk, latency delta, and cost delta
Signal pipeline ingesting weekly telemetry from model providers and internal usage (simulated ingestion if provider API absent)
Three deployment scenarios (best-case, constrained-capacity, price-shock) with quantified impact to per-token cost and P95 latency for two sample workloads
Runbook draft linking score thresholds to actions: alert Console, trigger Dedicated capacity bid, or enable automatic fallback variant
Prioritized research backlog (10 experiments) with owners, estimates, and success criteria
notes: Trade-offs discussed: deep quantitative modelling (longer but higher confidence) vs lightweight heuristics (faster, lower fidelity)

We will prioritize signals that are observable without vendor cooperation first: public release cadence, model download stats, open benchmark submissions, and latency measurements from public endpoints
Plan to include a 'graceful degradation' mapping for each model variant: which customer tier gets fallback, and what accuracy/regression tolerances are acceptable
Avoid building procurement automation in this sprint; focus on signal-to-action mappings and handoff to growth/ops for triggers
next_steps: Set up weekly 60-minute sync: attendees PM (Priya), Research (Ava Chen), Eng (Diego), Solutions (Michael O'Connor)
Prototype ingestion of three public signals (GitHub release cadence, Hugging Face model downloads, public latency probes) by 2026-03-05
Design scoring rubric and run 1st pass on 25 models by 2026-03-12
Schedule a cross-functional review with Sales/Customer Success to validate risk thresholds by 2026-03-20
